source.title: Stochastic Neural Network with Kronecker Flow
source.authors: Chin-Wei Huang; Ahmed Touati; P. Vincent; G. Dziugaite; Alexandre Lacoste; Aaron C. Courville

record.tranche_reason: Reports predictive test errors and PAC-Bayes bounds for stochastic Bayesian networks, extending generalization results to structured posterior methods; it does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test errors for variational Bayesian classifiers in Tables 1–2 and PAC-Bayes quantities in Table 3. These do not test any listed version: there is no random-label fit, width sweep, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout comparison, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or removal of memorized examples. Table 4 bandit regret is outside the claim. Cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates posterior families, predictive errors, PAC-Bayes bounds and bandit regret. It neither tests nor uses any listed claim version. Parameter perturbations are used to optimize posterior distributions and bounds, without testing V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps. Table 3 includes MLPs and LeNet, but does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures trained from scratch with standard gradient methods as V3 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but the relevant gap is between risk and its PAC-Bayes bound, rather than specifically empirical risk and the bound. The authors conclude that Kronecker Flow scales to larger architectures, is competitive with existing Bayesian methods, and tightens numerical PAC-Bayes bounds by capturing parameter dependencies.
record.recipe_differences: Studies stochastic Bayesian neural networks with variational objectives and PAC-Bayes bound minimization, rather than the standard gradient-trained deterministic networks or interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test errors differ by posterior family, dataset, architecture, and whether VGG-16 training uses data augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Posterior-family comparisons yield competitive predictive errors. K-Nonlinear reaches 0.60% on MNIST and 9.88% on augmented CIFAR-10; it does not win every condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured Bayesian weight distributions can improve predictive performance relative to simpler posterior families, depending on architecture and training setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports empirical risk, held-out risk, KL and numerical PAC-Bayes bounds. For the two-hidden-layer MLP under Catoni optimization, K-Nonlinear lowers the reported bound from Diag's 26.41% to 22.53%. This tests bound tightening, not magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capturing dependencies in Bayesian weight distributions can tighten numerical PAC-Bayes risk bounds.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics 2020 (PMLR volume 108)
record.problems: The predictive tables report test errors without training errors, so they do not quantify train–test gaps. The experiments use Bayesian/stochastic networks and do not test the claim's listed mechanisms. Table 1 notes K-Diag diverged on CIFAR-5 and omits that result.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports PAC-Bayes quantities and Table 4 reports contextual-bandit cumulative regret, neither of which is a train–test error result or one of the listed version measures. The missing K-Diag CIFAR-5 result is noted in Table 1 and is not a numeric result row.

untested.parts: No random-label training or comparison with natural-label training.
No width sweep across the interpolation threshold.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison under the specified training regime, or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison with matched tuning and model objectives; cited SGD baselines versus Bayesian posterior methods do not establish it.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or recipe adaptations.
No dropout addition, strength sweep, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. All listed numeric values match Tables 1–2, but fourteen rows reproduce external results. The absence of training errors applies to Tables 1–2; Table 3 does report empirical and held-out risks. Its results are already declared in rows_left_out and bear on no listed version, so they require no missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test-error behavior as width grows beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons to norm- and margin-based measures.
Effect of removing the most memorized training examples.
